markdown_report:
The best next step is a controlled diagnostic experiment testing whether recent-history sensitivity predicts useful SASRec interventions. At 10% progress, establishing that connection is more valuable than adding a complex architecture.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Electronics has a 14.95% sampled training reversal rate versus 3.03% for Movies_and_TV. This motivates category-specific hypotheses but does not establish validation performance. (2) Existing deletions change both content and positions. Their effects therefore cannot isolate reliance on recent evidence. (3) Users describe excessive reliance on broad resemblance and older interactions. These observations motivate recency tests, while compatibility and replacement intent remain unknown without supporting evidence.

**Insights from related work.** (1) Reported recency-weighted transition results motivate a simple recency intervention [1]. Their effectiveness on these Amazon datasets remains untested. (2) Positional-embedding research motivates separating item identity from position [2]. History-edit explanations measure sensitivity, which need not imply better recommendations [3]. (3) Sampled ranking metrics can reverse model comparisons [4]. The pinned HR@10 remains the selection objective, with no claim of improved full-catalog ranking.

**Framework and directions.** Organize experiments along three axes: evidence source (history identity, position, or observed text), intervention (probe-only or training change), and outcome (sensitivity or validation improvement). This separates mechanism diagnosis, evidence-grounded relevance auditing, and intervention validation. The key gap is evidence connecting a probe prediction to a successful training change.

**Candidate ideas.** Scores are originality/potential/difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

- **Position-controlled recency audit, 5/8/4:** Combines paired controls with prospective intervention predictions; established components limit novelty. It could support repeatable diagnosis, but small panels limit conclusions. Adapter changes are modest; positional confounding requires care [2,3].
- **Recency-weighted SASRec loss, 3/7/2:** Directly tests current-interest emphasis; weighting is conventional. It may improve relevance, but can discard durable preferences. Implementation is small; weight selection consumes validation budget [1].
- **Recency-weighted transition residual, 4/7/5:** Adds an interpretable transition signal; the combination is incremental. It could address sparse contextual learning, but popularity may dominate. Sparse counts are practical; synchronized inference adds work [1].

**Selected algorithm.** Freeze a training-user panel, candidates, replacement draws, and hypotheses before comparisons. Replace recent or old nonfinal history items with items matched by training frequency and embedding norm, keeping occupied positions and the final item fixed. Include unchanged histories and explicit position-swap probes; matching reduces measured confounds without eliminating semantic differences.

Record paired target-rank changes and within-category user-bootstrap intervals. Test unchanged SASRec against one preregistered recency-weighted loss setting; compare its validation gain with the diagnostic prediction and a shuffled-diagnostic assignment control. Retain preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, all four routes, and pinned macro HR@10. Conditional intervals quantify user uncertainty, not seed robustness or adaptive-selection bias. Preserve diagnostic interfaces, restore RNG/model state, and log every run within the shared budget.

idea.description: A position-controlled recency audit coupled to a preregistered SASRec loss intervention, testing whether measured history sensitivity predicts improvements in pinned macro validation HR@10.
idea.motivation: Existing history deletions confound item removal with positional shifts and changes to the final conditioning item. User feedback motivates testing recent evidence, but neither that feedback nor training margins establishes which intervention will improve validation ranking.
idea.implementation_notes: Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Return metrics and metric_definitions with eligibility counts, replacement-matching quality, uncertainty, and limitations. Use view.model as the trained module and retain architecture-compatible scoring hooks. Build probes from training histories only; never include their final training target in its conditioning prefix. Replace occupied nonfinal positions without introducing internal padding, exclude the original item and target from replacements, and keep candidate identities fixed across paired edits. Describe frequency/norm matching as partial control, not causal identification. For the training intervention use weighted BCE over valid positions, with preregistered weights increasing toward each sequence's latest valid target and normalized to mean one. Keep the original objective, sampler, and optimizer otherwise fixed. Preserve DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, all dataset routes, and the predictor writer; this loss-only change needs no inference architecture change. Produce full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for the required five training users per category. Treat compatibility, ratings, review text, categories, and simulator traits as unobserved. Budget all training and diagnostic execution within 43,200 GPU-seconds; honor SASREC_EPOCHS=200 unless explicitly changed and logged.
idea.pseudocode:
freeze panel, candidate sets, edits, hypotheses, and one recency-weight setting
save model modes and Python/NumPy/Torch RNG states
try:
    set view.model to eval
    under no_grad:
        for each required dataset and eligible training prefix:
            score unchanged prefix twice as determinism control
            replace matched recent and old nonfinal items at fixed positions
            score identical target-plus-negative candidates
            record paired rank changes, overlap, and matching residuals
        bootstrap paired users within each category
        report equal-category summaries only with complete coverage
finally:
    restore model modes and RNG states
return {metrics, metric_definitions}

train unchanged baseline with seed 42
train one preregistered recency-weighted valid-position BCE variant with seed 42
obtain pinned validation HR@10 through the unchanged host evaluator
compare paired category and macro gains with frozen diagnostic predictions
compare prediction agreement against shuffled diagnostic assignments
report all outcomes; label the small experiment exploratory

def diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    format measured metrics, definitions, controls, and limitations
    request testable interpretations without claiming unobserved preferences

originality.positive: Combines position-controlled perturbations with prospective tests of whether diagnostics identify beneficial interventions.
originality.negative: Perturbations, matched controls, recency weighting, and preregistration are established techniques; novelty lies mainly in their integration.

future_potential.positive: Could establish a reusable procedure for evaluating whether recommender diagnostics support effective model changes.
future_potential.negative: One intervention and four categories cannot establish general predictive validity, causal attribution, or training-seed robustness.

code_difficulty.positive: Reuses SASRec scoring and changes only valid-position loss weights during training.
code_difficulty.negative: Frozen manifests, replacement matching, positional bookkeeping, state restoration, and paired uncertainty estimates require careful implementation.

related_work.title: Do Sequential Recommendation Benchmarks Really Require Higher-Order Sequence Modelling?
contributions: [1] The supplied search summary reports competitive recency-weighted pairwise models, motivating simple recency and transition controls.
limitations: Reported benchmark results do not establish effectiveness on the four specified Amazon datasets.

related_work.title: Luo et al. (2024): positional embeddings in sequential recommendation
contributions: [2] The supplied summary identifies token-distance effects in learned positional embeddings, motivating separate content and position probes.
limitations: Positional sensitivity does not itself identify a beneficial training intervention.

related_work.title: Scarcelli et al. (2025): history-edit explanations
contributions: [3] Uses discrete history edits to investigate changes in recommendations.
limitations: Recommendation changes demonstrate model sensitivity rather than improved relevance or validation accuracy.

related_work.title: Krichene and Rendle: sampled recommendation metrics
contributions: [4] Shows that sampled evaluation can change model comparisons, motivating careful interpretation of the pinned candidate-based objective.
limitations: Does not provide evidence that the proposed diagnostics predict improvements or justify changing the host evaluator.
